findings.text: `n := int(nth)` is an unchecked narrowing or wrapping conversion. On 64-bit, `Nth(s, uint64(math.MaxUint64))` becomes -1 and silently returns the last element instead of an out-of-bounds error. `uint64(1<<63)` becomes MinInt, so `-n > l` is false (negating MinInt overflows) and `collection[l+n]` panics. On 32-bit, `int64(1<<32)` becomes 0 and returns element 0.

The signature now has a second type parameter `N`. Existing explicit instantiations such as `Nth[int](xs, 1)` no longer compile because `N` can't be inferred when only one type argument is supplied. This also breaks function-value uses like `f := lo.Nth[int]`. Separately, `constraints` must be imported in find.go. I couldn't confirm that, because the patch doesn't show the import block.

1.reason: Go accepts partial type-argument lists and infers the rest from the call, so `Nth[int](xs, 1)` still compiles (N is inferred as int from the untyped constant); losing function values like `lo.Nth[int]` comes with the intentional move to a generic index type rather than being a defect; and the import block can't be checked because ./context/ is missing, so only the patch was available.
